subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay on the accepted-then-async `sessions_spawn` contract with a terminal startup failure state, or should sandbox startup be preflighted before returning accepted?
rationale: Both shapes could fix the visible hang, but the choice affects lifecycle events, registry/session state, gateway wait behavior, and the overlapping startup-silence contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, session history, subagents list, and gateway wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation ahead of the accepted response to reject immediately, accepting latency and compatibility changes for existing callers.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox-specific proof case while maintainers first settle the broader startup lifecycle design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, session history, subagents list, and gateway wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest history across the `sessions_spawn`, sandbox, subagent lifecycle, and gateway surfaces affected by the decision.
